axis_source_rule: AXES COME FROM THE PREDICATE, NEVER FROM THE DESCRIPTION. A check's description is prose about the requirement; its predicate is the requirement as scored. Reading axes off descriptions invents obligations the suite never checks — see `sep-2575-http-server-unsupported-version-400`, whose description names 400 AND an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError and whose predicate is `S.status===400` alone.

extraction_procedure: 1. Locate the axis expression verbatim in the dist. Each of the seven used here occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file, so the location is unambiguous.
2. Walk back to the nearest enclosing `a(` check-emitting call (or, for the client-leg class-based scenario, the enclosing `getChecks(){`).
3. Balanced-scan forward to the matching close, honouring ' " ` string contexts and ${} template nesting, and record the span.
4. `evaluator_excerpt` is that span verbatim; `dist_byte_span` addresses it in the file named by `harness_dist_sha256`, so any reader with that build can re-cut it.
provenance.residual: Committed axes are a READING OF A PREDICATE AT ONE BUILD. A harness bump invalidates them exactly as A1's residual R3 says it invalidates keys. The sha is recorded so a reader can tell whether it has been invalidated; nothing here detects it automatically.

the_7_5_split.claim: A3's partial-axis ruling moves at most 7 of the 12, not 12. The other 5 move the OTHER way — into bucket 2, 'write the test', not 'extend the assertion'.
the_7_5_split.reasoning: For a SINGLE-axis check, 'we assert the code but not the status' is NO match, not a partial one: covering zero of one axis has nothing partial about it, and the code assertion is evidence about a DIFFERENT check (`RequestMetaInvalid`, `ServerUnsupportedVersionError`, `ServerRejectsUndeclaredCapability`), which is why those three also appear among server-stateless's 17 failures. Recording it as partial would credit us with coverage filed elsewhere.
the_7_5_split.status: PROVISIONAL. The OC side is measured here; the ET side is not swept until B2a. MES-65's 'A3's partial-axis ruling alone moves 12 checks between buckets' is superseded by this and the PM will correct the epic body once B2a confirms.

what_this_is: The per-check AXIS DECOMPOSITION the match relation's `partial` ruling is computed from. An OC check's predicate is a conjunction of axes; against each axis an ET claim is exactly one of agrees/contradicts/silent. This file records the axes, each as a verbatim substring of the evaluator it was read from.
